captions.detailed: A computer-controlled GoTo Newtonian reflector telescope mounted on a single-arm robotic fork mount. The beige/cream cylindrical optical tube is held by two black ring cradles and features a small grey finder scope near the eyepiece end. The dark grey single-arm mount stands on a circular base with three short stabilizing feet, allowing continuous 360-degree horizontal rotation (azimuth joint) and vertical tilting (altitude joint) of the telescope tube.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a computerized GoTo reflector telescope on a single-arm fork mount. It should feature a cylindrical optical tube with mounting rings, connected via a revolute altitude joint to a vertical fork arm, which rotates on a continuous azimuth joint relative to a three-legged circular base.
captions.factory: Construct the base using a flat cylinder combined with three radial rectangular boxes for the feet. Build the rotating azimuth motor housing as a stacked cylinder on top of the base. Model the single fork arm as a tall vertical box, and attach a cylindrical altitude joint hub near its top. Finally, construct the telescope tube using a long hollowed cylinder, wrapped in two thin ring-shaped cylinders connected by a support bar, and mount it to the altitude joint.
